'''''Geranium columbinum''''', common name '''long-stalked crane's-bill'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> or '''longstalk cranesbill''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=GECO|taxon=Geranium columbinum|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref> is a [[herbaceous]] [[annual plant]] in the family [[Geraniaceae]].

==Description==
[[File:Geraniaceae - Geranium columbinum-2.JPG|thumb|240px|right|Close-up of a flower of ''Geranium columbinum'']]
''Geranium columbinum'' reaches on average {{convert|15|-|30|cm}} in height, with a maximum of {{convert|60|cm}}.<ref name=Pignatti>Pignatti S. - Flora d'Italia – Edagricole – 1982. Vol. II, pag. 10</ref> The stem is more or less erect, hairy and quite branched. The leaves are opposite, approximately pentagonal and palmate and the leaf lobes have two to three deep cuts making it similar in shape to a pigeon's foot (hence the Latin epithet ''columbinus'').  The flowers are pink to purple, {{convert|15|-|20|mm}} in size,<ref name=Pignatti/> with five obovate-heart-shaped petals as long as the sepals. The petals are 7–9 mm long, with distinctive veining. The flowering period extends from March to September.<ref name=Pignatti/> The flowers are [[Glossary of botanical terms|hermaphrodite]] and pollinated by insects ([[entomogamy]]).

==Distribution==
This plant is present throughout Europe, Western Asia and Northern Africa.<ref name=Tela/> It has also been introduced into North America.

==Habitat==
''Geranium columbinum'' prefers moderately dry, nutrient-rich calcareous soils, in woods, hedgerows and roadsides, at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1200|m}} above sea level.<ref name=Pignatti/>
